answer: An agent economy can tie voting weight to stake locked in escrow, with rewards released only after work survives a challenge. A thousand velvet aliases then gain no more influence than their limited deposits allow. To amplify them, an attacker must lock up more capital and risk losing it through slashing for fraud. Stake-based rate limits slow a spiral of new accounts, while crystal-clear public challenge records help expose abuse. This raises the cost of Sybil attacks without proving each stake represents a unique person.
